dev: The neural tube — baby’s future brain and spinal cord — is beginning to form.
Implantation into the womb lining is complete.
The placenta is starting to develop.
body: You may have just missed your period.
Early tiredness and tender breasts are common.
4.normal: A missed period and mild cramping are completely normal now — your body is quietly getting to work.
4.faith: Begin with a niyyah — a quiet du’a of gratitude for this amanah (trust) placed in your care.
4.tip: Take 400 micrograms of folic acid every day until 12 weeks, and 10 micrograms of vitamin D.

dev: A tiny heart begins to beat.
The earliest blood vessels are forming.
Layers that will become organs are developing.
body: Nausea may begin and your sense of smell can sharpen.
You might feel more tired than usual.
5.normal: Waves of nausea and sudden tiredness are normal — rest whenever you can.
5.faith: Say Bismillah before eating and drinking — nourishing baby with what is halal and tayyib.
5.tip: Sip water often and keep plain crackers by the bed for morning sickness.

dev: Facial features and limb buds are forming.
The heart is beating steadily now.
The brain is developing rapidly.
body: Fatigue and more frequent trips to the loo are common.
Breasts may feel fuller and more sensitive.
6.normal: Needing the loo more often is normal — your blood flow is increasing.
6.faith: Keep your tongue moist with dhikr — “SubhanAllah wa bihamdihi” through the day.
6.tip: Rest when you can — growing a person is real work.

dev: The brain is developing fast.
Hands and feet look like tiny paddles.
Kidneys are getting ready to work.
body: Nausea may peak now, along with mood shifts.
Food aversions can come and go.
7.normal: Mood swings are normal — pregnancy hormones are rising quickly.
7.faith: The Ahlulbayt (as) encouraged reciting Qur’an aloud so baby hears it — start with short surahs.
7.tip: Small, frequent meals ease sickness better than large ones.

dev: Arms and legs are getting longer, and hands and feet are forming.
Tiny movements begin, though you can’t feel them yet.
Baby’s heartbeat is strong.
body: Bloating and breast changes are common.
You may notice more saliva or a metallic taste.
8.normal: A metallic taste and extra saliva are odd but normal early signs.
8.faith: Recite Surah al-Fatiha over your water and drink it with a calm heart.
8.tip: Book your first midwife (booking) appointment if you haven’t.

dev: All the major organs are in place and developing.
The heartbeat is strong and steady.
Baby is starting to look more human.
body: Waistbands feel tighter; tiredness lingers.
Headaches can come with hormone changes.
9.normal: Mild headaches are common — rest, water and fresh air often help.
9.faith: Give a small sadaqah for baby’s wellbeing — even a coin set aside daily.
9.tip: Gentle walking helps digestion and lifts your mood.

dev: Now called a foetus rather than an embryo.
Vital organs are already working.
Tiny nails are starting to form.
body: For many, nausea starts to ease from here.
You may feel bloated as digestion slows.
10.normal: Slower digestion and bloating are normal — fibre and water help.
10.faith: Recite Ayatul Kursi morning and night for protection.
10.tip: Keep hydrated: aim for 6 to 8 glasses of fluid a day.

dev: Fingers and toes separate.
Tooth buds are appearing.
Baby can open and close their fists.
body: Your appetite may be returning.
Skin may look brighter as blood flow rises.
11.normal: A returning appetite is a welcome, normal sign the first trimester is easing.
11.faith: The Ahlulbayt (as) praised quince (safarjal) — narrated to gladden the heart.
11.tip: Add fruit and fibre to help ease constipation.

dev: Reflexes are developing — baby can curl fingers and toes.
Kidneys begin producing urine.
Vital systems are all in place.
body: The end of the first trimester is near.
Nausea often begins to fade.
12.normal: Feeling more like yourself again is normal as hormones settle.
12.faith: A du’a of shukr — the hardest weeks are passing, alhamdulillah.
12.tip: Your dating scan is offered between 10 and 14 weeks.

dev: Fingerprints are forming.
Vocal cords are developing.
Baby’s intestines move into the abdomen.
body: Energy often returns this week.
Your waistline may be thickening.
13.normal: A rise in energy is normal — enjoy it, but don’t overdo things.
13.faith: Recite Surah Yusuf — traditionally read for a child of beauty and good character.
13.tip: Start thinking about comfortable, roomier clothing.

dev: Baby can squint, frown and grimace.
Fine hair (lanugo) is forming.
The liver and spleen start working.
body: Welcome to the second trimester — often the “golden” phase.
Aches from stretching ligaments may appear.
14.normal: Mild aches as things stretch are normal — gentle movement eases them.
14.faith: Keep wudhu when you can; a state of purity is its own comfort.
14.tip: Gentle stretching eases back and hip aches.

dev: Baby can sense light through closed eyelids.
Fine hair is growing all over.
Baby is moving lots, though you may not feel it yet.
body: Your bump may be starting to show.
Nasal congestion is common in pregnancy.
15.normal: A stuffy nose (“pregnancy rhinitis”) is a normal, harmless nuisance.
15.faith: Speak kindly and avoid anger — a mother’s calm state nourishes her baby.
15.tip: Keep moving daily; swimming is gentle and wonderful now.

dev: Baby can hear muffled sounds.
The heart is pumping lots of blood each day.
Facial muscles let baby make expressions.
body: You may feel the first flutters soon.
Skin and hair often look their best now.
16.normal: First flutters (“quickening”) can feel like bubbles — totally normal.
16.faith: Recite Qur’an and talk to your baby — they are beginning to hear you.
16.tip: Sleep on your side as your bump grows.

dev: Fat stores are beginning to form.
The skeleton is hardening from cartilage to bone.
Baby’s sense of hearing is sharpening.
body: Appetite is up as your bump grows.
You may feel warmer than usual.
17.normal: Feeling hotter is normal — your blood volume and metabolism are up.
17.faith: Eat dates — beloved of the Prophet (s) and full of goodness.
17.tip: Iron-rich foods help as your blood volume rises.

dev: Baby is yawning, hiccupping and stretching.
Ears are in their final position.
A protective layer of myelin forms around nerves.
body: You may feel baby move any time between 16 and 24 weeks, often after 20 with a first baby.
You may notice mild dizziness at times.
18.normal: Occasional dizziness is normal — rise slowly and stay hydrated.
18.faith: Give thanks at each movement — a sign of life and a gift.
18.tip: Your anomaly scan is usually between 18 and 21 weeks.

dev: A protective coating (vernix) now covers the skin.
The brain is developing areas for the senses.
Baby has regular sleep and wake times.
body: Round ligament aches are common as things stretch.
Leg cramps may start, especially at night.
19.normal: Sharp, brief aches down the sides of your bump are normal ligament stretching.
19.faith: Recite Surah Maryam — narrated for ease in pregnancy and delivery.
19.tip: Whooping cough vaccine: you can have it from 16 weeks and it’s usually offered around 20. Ask your midwife or GP if you haven’t been offered it.

dev: You may feel the first flutters of movement — quickening.
Baby is developing a sleep-and-wake rhythm.
A protective coating (vernix) now covers the skin.
body: First kicks, mild backache and occasional heartburn.
Your bump is clearly showing now.
20.normal: Those first flutters are a quiet conversation between you and baby — pause and enjoy them.
20.faith: A halfway du’a — thank Allah and ask for a safe rest of the journey.
20.tip: Pelvic floor exercises now really pay off later.

dev: Eyebrows and eyelids are fully formed.
Baby’s movements are becoming stronger.
The digestive system is practising for milk.
body: Kicks are getting stronger.
You may notice stretch marks appearing.
21.normal: Stretch marks are normal and very common — moisturising can ease itching.
21.faith: Pomegranate is praised in narrations — eat it with the niyyah of a good-natured child.
21.tip: Ask your midwife for your MAT B1 maternity certificate; it’s issued from 20 weeks.

dev: Baby’s sense of touch is developing.
Fine details like eyebrows are visible.
Baby is starting to look like a newborn.
body: You may notice practice (Braxton Hicks) tightenings.
Swollen feet and ankles can appear.
22.normal: Painless tightenings that come and go are normal practice contractions.
22.faith: Read a portion of Qur’an aloud daily — a rhythm baby will recognise after birth.
22.tip: Rest your legs to ease any swelling.

dev: Tiny blood vessels in the lungs are developing.
Baby can hear your voice and heartbeat clearly.
Skin is still wrinkled as fat fills in.
body: Skin changes like the linea nigra may appear.
Your bump feels firmer and higher.
23.normal: A dark line down the belly (linea nigra) is normal and usually fades after birth.
23.faith: Keep a daily dhikr — the tasbih of Sayyida Fatima (as) after each salah.
23.tip: Stay gently active to help sleep and mood.

dev: A viability milestone — a big developmental marker.
The inner ear is now fully formed, aiding balance.
Lungs are developing branches and cells.
body: Your bump is measured at check-ups from around now.
Backache is common as your posture shifts.
24.normal: A growing lower-back ache is normal — supportive shoes and good posture help.
24.faith: Sadaqah wards off harm — give with the intention of protection for baby.
24.tip: If you have a risk factor for gestational diabetes, such as south Asian heritage, your glucose test is due between 24 and 28 weeks.

dev: Baby is responding to the sound of your voice.
Hands are now fully developed and active.
Baby is gaining baby fat, smoothing the skin.
body: Backache and a bigger appetite are common.
Hands may tingle (carpal tunnel) at times.
25.normal: Mild tingling in the hands is a normal effect of pregnancy swelling.
25.faith: Say your du’as and salawat aloud — baby’s hearing is sharpening.
25.tip: Support your lower back when sitting.

dev: Baby’s eyes will start to open soon.
Lungs are producing surfactant to help breathing later.
Brain activity is increasing.
body: You may feel pressure in your ribs and back.
Braxton Hicks may become more noticeable.
26.normal: Rib pressure as baby grows upward is normal — gentle stretches give relief.
26.faith: Recite Surah al-Mulk at night — a surah of protection.
26.tip: Practise slow, deep breathing to relax.

dev: Sleep-wake cycles are forming and baby hiccups often.
The brain is very active now.
Baby can open and close their eyes.
body: The third trimester begins.
Tiredness and heartburn may return.
27.normal: Feeling more tired again as you enter the third trimester is completely normal.
27.faith: Renew your niyyah for the final stretch — patience (sabr) is worship.

dev: Baby’s eyes can now open and blink.
Eyelashes have formed.
Baby is adding fat and muscle steadily.
body: Braxton Hicks may be more noticeable.
Shortness of breath can come as baby grows.
28.normal: Getting a little breathless is normal — your lungs have less room now.
28.faith: The book recommends frankincense (kundur), chewed by the mother — linked in narrations to the child’s intelligence and memory.
28.tip: At 28 weeks you’ll be offered the RSV vaccine, a blood test for iron, and anti-D if you’re rhesus negative. From now, go to sleep on your side.

dev: Muscles and lungs are maturing.
Baby’s head is growing to fit the developing brain.
Bones are fully formed but still soft.
body: Heartburn and tiredness may increase.
You may need the loo more as baby presses down.
29.normal: More frequent loo trips are normal as baby settles lower.
29.faith: Recite Ayatul Kursi and gently blow over yourself and your bump.

dev: Baby is gaining fat and the brain is growing quickly.
Bone marrow now makes red blood cells.
Baby’s grip is getting stronger.
body: You may feel more short of breath.
Sleep can become harder to find.
30.normal: Broken sleep is normal now — nap when you can and use pillows for support.
30.faith: A gratitude note a day keeps the heart soft.
30.tip: Prop yourself up with pillows to sleep.

dev: All five senses are now working.
Baby can turn their head from side to side.
The brain is making rapid connections.
body: Frequent urination often returns.
Your breasts may start to leak colostrum.
31.normal: A little leaking of early milk (colostrum) is a normal sign your body is preparing.
31.faith: Send salawat upon Muhammad and his family — a light for mother and child.
31.tip: Start lightly packing your hospital bag.

dev: Baby is practising breathing movements.
Toenails and fingernails have formed.
Baby likely settles into a head-down position soon.
body: Your bump sits high with less room inside.
Braxton Hicks may feel stronger.
32.normal: Stronger practice contractions are normal — rest and hydration usually settle them.
32.faith: Recite Surah Yasin — known as the heart of the Qur’an.
32.tip: Keep monitoring baby’s movements each day.

dev: Bones are hardening (except the soft skull plates).
The immune system is building with your antibodies.
Baby’s pupils can respond to light.
body: Aches and tiredness are common.
You may feel warm and swollen.
33.normal: Some swelling in feet and hands is normal — raise your feet when you rest.
33.faith: Begin the du’as for a safe and easy delivery now.
33.tip: Rest often and conserve your energy.

dev: Baby is often head-down now.
The central nervous system is maturing.
Lungs are nearly ready for the first breath.
body: Swelling and fatigue may increase.
Pelvic pressure can build as baby drops.
34.normal: A feeling of pressure low down is normal as baby moves into position.
34.faith: Increase sadaqah as delivery nears — protection for a safe birth.
34.tip: Learn the warning signs and when to call your midwife.

dev: Kidneys and liver are working well.
Baby is gaining weight quickly now.
Most development is complete — mainly growing now.
body: Your bump feels heavy and full.
You may feel Braxton Hicks more often.
35.normal: Feeling large and slow is normal — listen to your body and rest.
35.faith: Recite Surah al-Inshiqaq — narrated to ease childbirth.

dev: Likely head-down and settling into position.
Baby is shedding the vernix and lanugo.
The digestive system is ready for milk.
body: Baby may “drop”, easing your breathing.
You may feel more pressure on your bladder.
36.normal: Easier breathing but more loo trips is normal once baby drops (“lightening”).
36.faith: Keep dates nearby — echoing Maryam (as), who ate them near delivery.

dev: Baby is now considered early term.
Practising breathing, sucking and gripping.
The brain and lungs continue to mature.
body: Pelvic pressure and a nesting urge are common.
You may notice more discharge.
37.normal: A sudden burst of energy to tidy and prepare (nesting) is a normal late sign.
37.faith: A du’a of tawakkul — place your trust in Allah for the birth.

dev: A firm grasp and organs ready for life outside.
Baby’s skin is now smooth.
Baby is building the last of their fat stores.
body: Waiting mode; tiredness is normal.
You may feel cramps or a dull backache.
38.normal: A come-and-go backache and cramps are normal as your body prepares.
38.faith: Recite Surah Maryam and Surah al-Inshiqaq for ease.
38.tip: Know the early signs of labour.

dev: Baby is full term and building a little more fat.
Lungs are ready to breathe air.
The brain is still growing rapidly.
body: Cramps and a “show” may appear.
You may feel period-like tightenings.
39.normal: Losing the mucus plug (a “show”) is a normal sign labour may be near.
39.faith: Continuous dhikr and salawat keep the heart steady.
39.tip: Eat dates daily, the food of Maryam (as) in labour (19:25) and narrated for the month of birth.

dev: Baby is ready to meet you — everything is in place.
The soft skull plates allow an easier birth.
Baby is fully developed.
body: Labour could begin any time now.
You may feel strong, regular tightenings.
40.normal: Going a little past your due date is normal — most babies arrive within a week or two.
40.faith: A mother’s du’a at this time is precious — ask freely, for yourself and your child.
40.tip: Call your maternity unit when contractions are strong and regular, if your waters break, if you bleed, or if baby moves less.

dev: The growth spurt is essentially over; baby is fully ready for life outside.
Overdue babies often have dry, peeling skin — normal, from losing the vernix.
Everything is in place; baby is simply waiting.
body: Your care team will offer a membrane sweep, then discuss monitoring or induction.
Braxton Hicks and late-pregnancy symptoms carry on.
41.normal: Going past your due date is normal and common, especially with a first baby.
41.faith: Keep to your daily salawat and istighfar, and ask freely — these are precious days.
41.tip: Stay aware of your baby’s usual pattern. If movements slow down, change or stop, call your maternity unit straight away, day or night.

1.note: Your body is quietly getting to work. Some women feel PMS-like symptoms, pressure, tender breasts or implantation spotting; others feel nothing at all, which is just as normal.

acts.t: Adhān and iqāmah before every prayer
acts.s: With your hand on your stomach. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.110.
Then blow gently on your stomach. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.109.
Recite once, blow on the dates, eat them on an empty stomach. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.110.

acts.t: A sweet apple in the morning
acts.s: Apple on an empty stomach is praised in Makārim al-Akhlāq, p.173. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.109.
On an empty stomach. Imām al-Kāẓim (as): a pomegranate eaten on Friday before food lights the heart for forty mornings. al-Kāfī, Vol. 6, p.355.

acts.t: A tiny amount of Khāke Shifāʾ before sunset
acts.s: No bigger than a lentil, with the intention of shifāʾ. Sistani allows eating the turbah of Imām Ḥusayn (as) only up to a chickpea’s size, for healing (Islamic Laws, ruling 2645). Soil can carry toxoplasmosis (NHS), so tell your midwife you take it. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.110.
Folic acid, 400 micrograms a day until 12 weeks. Choose a pregnancy multivitamin: ordinary ones and cod liver oil can contain vitamin A (retinol), which is not safe in pregnancy. NHS.

The NHS advises a 10 microgram supplement every day from October to March, and all year if you usually cover most of your skin outdoors. UK milk is not usually fortified, so food alone will not cover it.

1.activity: Walking, stretching and yoga are gentle ways to start, and worth keeping up through the pregnancy. The NHS suggests building up to 150 minutes a week; you should still be able to hold a conversation while you exercise.

2.note: Webbed hands and feet, nose and eyelids beginning to form. Nausea, food aversions or cravings may step up, and bloating can make the belly look a little bigger already.

acts.s: With wa ʿajjil farajahum at the end. The ṣalawāt from Thursday ʿAṣr to Friday is in Biḥār al-Anwār, Vol. 86, p.289; the count of 140: From Marriage to Parenthood, p.110.
With wa ʿajjil farajahum at the end. Saying it 100 times on Friday: Biḥār al-Anwār, Vol. 86, p.289.

acts.t: The long ṣalawāt, hand on your stomach
acts.s: The words are in Biḥār al-Anwār, Vol. 86, p.289, as a Thursday and Friday ṣalawāt. The hand on your stomach: From Marriage to Parenthood, p.110.
From Marriage to Parenthood, p.110.

acts.t: Sūrah al-Ikhlāṣ (112) over two jujube dates
acts.s: Eat them on an empty stomach. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.111.

acts.t: Meat with sweet apple, and milk
acts.s: Once a week is enough for these. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.110.

2.activity: If you were not active before pregnancy, do not suddenly take up anything strenuous. Start with 10 minutes a day, perhaps a brisk walk, and warm up before and cool down after. Stop if you feel exhausted or too breathless to talk.

3.note: Key body systems and vital organs are developing, and the digestive system starts working by the end of the trimester. You may hear the heartbeat at your next appointment. Dizziness, a sharper sense of smell and frequent bathroom trips are common.

acts.s: With wa ʿajjil farajahum at the end. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.111.

acts.t: The long ṣalawāt, hand on your stomach
acts.s: Before each prayer. Same wording as last month (Biḥār al-Anwār, Vol. 86, p.289); the hand on your stomach: From Marriage to Parenthood, p.111.
From Marriage to Parenthood, p.111.
Then eat it on an empty stomach. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.111.
From Marriage to Parenthood, p.111.
Once a week is enough for these. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.111.

3.activity: Start pelvic floor exercises. They help stop leaks when you cough, sneeze or laugh, now and after the birth. Squeeze the muscles you would use to stop a wee and hold in wind, a few quick squeezes first, then slow ones held for up to 10 seconds. Aim for 3 sets of 8 squeezes a day; a set at each meal helps you remember.

4.note: Eyes are working, facial muscles can make expressions and fingerprints are forming. Expect weight gain and a more pronounced belly, and possibly a blocked nose, bleeding gums, backache and more discharge. Imām ʿAlī (as) said to name children before they are born (al-Kāfī, Vol. 6, p.18); aim to choose by four months and ten days.

acts.s: The prayer for comfort in your family. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.112.
Astaghfirullāha Rabbī wa atūbu ilayh. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.112.
From Marriage to Parenthood, p.112.
As much as you can manage. Sistani allows it any time after ʿIshāʾ until Fajr (Islamic Laws, ruling 760); if you miss it, make it up later. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.113.
From Marriage to Parenthood, p.111.

acts.t: Sūrah al-Qadr (97) in one rakʿah of every prayer
acts.s: After al-Fātiḥah, in the first or second rakʿah. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.112.

acts.t: After the daily prayers: al-Kawthar, al-Qadr, long ṣalawāt
acts.s: Sūrah al-Kawthar (108), Sūrah al-Qadr (97), then the long ṣalawāt with your hand on your stomach. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.112.
Eat them on an empty stomach. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.113.
Sweet pomegranate “improves the child”: al-Kāfī, Vol. 6, p.355. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.112.
Lentils and beans, wholegrains, cheese and yoghurt, and leafy greens (NHS).

4.activity: Gentle yoga and Pilates help with back pain and body aches. Use a qualified teacher who knows you are pregnant, and ask your midwife if you have concerns.

5.note: More lung development, and at the 20-week scan you may be able to find out the baby’s sex, if you want to and if your hospital tells parents. Expect hair and nail growth, a bigger appetite and the odd leg cramp.

acts.t: Rub Khāke Shifāʾ on your stomach
acts.s: From the start of the fifth month. Turbah from Karbalāʾ. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.113.

acts.t: Adhān and iqāmah at ṣalāh time
acts.s: With your hand on your stomach. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.113.
From Marriage to Parenthood, p.113.

acts.t: Sūrah an-Naṣr (110) in the daily prayers
acts.s: From Marriage to Parenthood, p.113.
Then eat it on an empty stomach. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.113.
Dates on an empty stomach are praised in Makārim al-Akhlāq, p.169. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.113.
Good fats, protein and vitamin E. Nuts are safe in pregnancy unless you are allergic or have been told to avoid them (NHS).

5.activity: Most exercise is safe in pregnancy if you go carefully and listen to your body. Swimming, brisk walking, a static bike, cross-trainer and low-impact classes are all good. Avoid lying flat on your back for long, contact sports and anything with a risk of falling.

6.note: Facial features are more defined, hearing is developing fast and eyelashes are coming through. Your belly button may pop out for a while, and carpal tunnel symptoms can appear. If you have a risk factor for gestational diabetes (south Asian heritage is one, as are a BMI over 30 or a parent or sibling with diabetes), you will be offered a glucose tolerance test between weeks 24 and 28.

acts.t: Rub Khāke Shifāʾ on your stomach after every prayer
acts.s: Turbah from Karbalāʾ. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.113.
Reciting al-Wāqiʿah on Friday is in Biḥār al-Anwār, Vol. 86, p.289; Thursday and this month: From Marriage to Parenthood, p.113.

acts.t: Sūrah at-Tīn (95) in one rakʿah of Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ
acts.s: From Marriage to Parenthood, p.113.
From Marriage to Parenthood, p.113.

6.activity: Most exercise is safe in pregnancy if you go carefully and listen to your body. Swimming, brisk walking, a static bike, cross-trainer and low-impact classes are all good. Avoid lying flat on your back for long, contact sports and anything with a risk of falling.

7.note: Better breathing, hiccups and blinking, and the beginnings of sleep cycles. Baby may start moving into position for birth over the coming weeks. You may get sciatica, a stuffy nose, faintness or dizziness, and bloating.

acts.s: From Marriage to Parenthood, p.114.

acts.t: Sūrah al-Anʿām (6) over almonds after Fajr
acts.s: For forty days, then eat the almonds. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.114.
From Marriage to Parenthood, p.114.
Often, from this month onward. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.114.

acts.t: The five sūrahs after your prayers
acts.s: After the daily prayers and the tasbīḥ of Sayyidah Fāṭimah (as): al-Ḥadīd (57), al-Ḥashr (59), aṣ-Ṣaff (61), al-Jumuʿah (62) and at-Taghābun (64). From Marriage to Parenthood, p.114.

acts.t: Sūrah al-Qadr (97) and al-Ikhlāṣ (112) in the daily prayers
acts.s: After al-Fātiḥah. Once you start al-Ikhlāṣ, finish it rather than switching (Sistani, Islamic Laws, ruling 974). From Marriage to Parenthood, p.114.
Then eat it on an empty stomach. Quince for pregnant women: al-Kāfī, Vol. 6, p.22. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.114.

After food rather than on an empty stomach (Imām al-ʿAskarī (as), Mustadrak al-Wasāʾil, Vol. 16, p.410). The pregnancy hadith, in Mustadrak Vol. 15, p.214, comes from a Sunni medical collection, so it is weak. Avoid water with it.
From Marriage to Parenthood, p.114.
Red meat, beans and chickpeas, nuts, dried apricots and fortified cereals. Your iron is checked at booking and at 28 weeks, and you’ll be offered a supplement if it is low (NHS).

7.activity: Keep going with walking, swimming and yoga. Only do what feels comfortable, and stop anything that adds to the discomfort. Ask your midwife if you have concerns.

8.note: Every organ is developed except the lungs, which are practising breathing, and the skin is no longer transparent. Expect Braxton Hicks tightenings, itchy skin over the bump, leaking colostrum, leg cramps and possibly piles or constipation.

acts.t: Adhān and iqāmah before every prayer
acts.s: With your hand on your stomach. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.114.

acts.t: Sūrah al-Qadr (97) ten times after Fajr
acts.s: From Marriage to Parenthood, p.115.
From Marriage to Parenthood, p.115.
From Marriage to Parenthood, p.115.

From Marriage to Parenthood, p.115.
From Marriage to Parenthood, p.115.
From Marriage to Parenthood, p.115.

acts.t: A sweet pomegranate on an empty stomach
acts.s: On an empty stomach. al-Kāfī, Vol. 6, p.355: a pomegranate on Friday before food lights the heart, and sweet pomegranate “improves the child”.
Once a week, if you have no fear of harm from it. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.115.

8.activity: Keep going with walking, swimming and yoga. Only do what feels comfortable, and stop anything that adds to the discomfort. Ask your midwife if you have concerns.

9.note: Hearing is very sharp now and baby may recognise your voice. Expect a waddling walk as baby drops into the pelvis, and pelvic pain with it. The guide ends at month nine, so this block covers the remaining weeks up to 41.

acts.s: Allāhumma ṣalli ʿalā Muḥammadin wa Āli Muḥammad.
Astaghfirullāha Rabbī wa atūbu ilayh. The Prophet (s) sought forgiveness seventy times a day (al-Kāfī, Vol. 2, p.505).
In the Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr prayers, one in each of the first two rakʿahs. adh-Dhāriyāt is long, so leave it out if time is short (Sistani, ruling 965). From Marriage to Parenthood, p.115.
From Marriage to Parenthood, p.115.
On Friday night, which is Thursday evening after Maghrib. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.115.

acts.t: Sūrah al-Insān (76) over dates and milk
acts.s: Then take them on an empty stomach. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.115.
“Feed women dates in the month they give birth, and their child will be forbearing and pure.” The Prophet (s), in Makārim al-Akhlāq, p.169. Kebabs: From Marriage to Parenthood, p.115.
Any amount helps; the NHS says 30 minutes a day can be enough.

also: Go easy on very spicy, rich or fatty food, which can bring on heartburn (NHS). From Marriage to Parenthood, p.115, says no garam masala.
Sacrifice a sheep as ṣadaqah on behalf of Imām al-Mahdī (aj), and eat from it. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.115; no hadith found.
Try to avoid looking into the mirror, and at pictures. From Marriage to Parenthood, p.115; no hadith found.
9.activity: A daily walk is the main recommendation this month. Ask your midwife if you have concerns.

sunnah.name: Quince (Safarjal)
sunnah.note: Imam al-Ṣādiq (as): a pregnant woman should eat quince so her child is sweeter-smelling and fairer. It also lifts grief. (al-Kāfī, Vol. 6)

sunnah.name: Dates (Tamr)
sunnah.note: Fresh dates at the birth, as Allah told Maryam (as); narrated to make the child forbearing. (al-Kāfī, Vol. 6)

sunnah.name: Pomegranate (Rumman)
sunnah.note: Sweet pomegranate is narrated to make the child good; one on an empty stomach on a Friday lights the heart. (al-Kāfī, Vol. 6)

sunnah.name: Apple (Tuffah)
sunnah.note: Narrated to cleanse the stomach, and in Ḥilyat al-Muttaqīn to make the child beautiful. (al-Kāfī, Vol. 6; From Marriage to Parenthood, p.102)

sunnah.name: Grapes (‘Inab)
sunnah.note: Narrated to lift sorrow: a prophet who complained of grief was told to eat grapes. (al-Kāfī, Vol. 6)

sunnah.name: Frankincense (Kundur)
sunnah.note: The Prophet (s) said to give pregnant women frankincense (lubān): it strengthens the child’s heart and adds to its intellect. (al-Kāfī, Vol. 6) It is a herbal remedy, so check with your midwife or pharmacist first (NHS).

sunnah.name: Milk (Laban)
sunnah.note: The food of the messengers; Imam al-Ṣādiq (as) said it builds flesh and strengthens bone. (al-Kāfī, Vol. 6)

sunnah.name: Honey (‘Asal)
sunnah.note: “Healing for people” (16:69); nothing heals like honey, said Imam al-Ṣādiq (as). Never give it to babies under one (NHS).

med.name: Iron-rich foods
med.note: Lean meat, beans & lentils support rising blood volume.

med.name: Protein
med.note: Eggs, beans and lean meat for steady growth.

med.name: Oily fish (low-mercury)
med.note: Omega-3 for brain and eyes. Aim for 2 portions of fish a week, one of them oily, and no more than 2 oily portions.

med.name: Water
med.note: Aim for 6 to 8 glasses a day, more in hot weather.

avoid.name: Raw or undercooked meat, game and some eggs
avoid.note: Cook meat until there is no pink. Avoid game such as venison and pheasant. British Lion eggs are fine runny; other eggs should be cooked hard.

avoid.name: Unpasteurised milk, and soft ripened or blue cheese
avoid.note: Listeria risk. Brie, camembert and soft blue cheese are fine cooked until steaming hot. Hard cheeses like cheddar are fine.

avoid.name: High-mercury fish
avoid.note: Avoid shark, swordfish and marlin. No more than 4 cans or 2 steaks of tuna a week. No raw fish or raw shellfish.

avoid.name: Liver & high-dose vitamin A
avoid.note: Too much vitamin A can harm baby. That includes liver pâté, cod liver oil and supplements containing retinol.

avoid.name: Alcohol
avoid.note: No amount is considered safe in pregnancy.

avoid.name: Excess caffeine
avoid.note: Keep under 200mg a day. A mug of instant coffee is about 100mg and a mug of tea about 75mg; coffee-shop coffee has more.

avoid.name: Smoking & shisha
avoid.note: Best avoided completely for baby’s health.

Pregnancy.title: Surah Yusuf
Pregnancy.translit: Recite Surah Yusuf (chapter 12) through the pregnancy. Some also recite it over an apple and eat it.
Pregnancy.body: A devotional practice from the compilations, not a narration.
Pregnancy.src: A Mother’s Prayer, ch.2, prayer 8; From Marriage to Parenthood, p.116

Pregnancy.title: Surah Maryam
Pregnancy.body: Recited daily through pregnancy, asking for a righteous and pious child.
Pregnancy.src: A Mother’s Prayer, ch.3, prayer 1; From Marriage to Parenthood, p.116

Pregnancy.title: Ayatul Kursi
Pregnancy.arabic: اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ
Pregnancy.body: A powerful ayah of protection. Recite morning and evening over yourself and your bump.
Pregnancy.src: Qurʾān 2:255; A Mother’s Prayer, ch.2, prayer 2; al-Kāfī, Vol. 6, Kitāb al-ʿAqīqah, ch.5 ḥ.1 (Imam al-Ṣādiq (as): recite it in the fourth month)

Pregnancy.title: Du’a for a righteous child
Pregnancy.arabic: رَبِّ هَبْ لِي مِنْ لَدُنْكَ ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةً
Pregnancy.translit: Rabbi hab lī min ladunka dhurriyyatan ṭayyibah
Pregnancy.body: “My Lord! Grant me a good offspring from You!” The prayer of Zakariyya (as) for a righteous child.
Pregnancy.src: Sūrah Āl ʿImrān 3:38 · From Marriage to Parenthood, p.117

Pregnancy.title: Surah al-Mulk
Pregnancy.body: Imam al-Bāqir (as) called it the protector; reciting it at night is a great good deed.
Pregnancy.src: al-Kāfī, Vol. 2, Kitāb Faḍl al-Qurʾān, ḥ.26 (Imam al-Bāqir)

Pregnancy.title: Surah al-Qadr
Pregnancy.translit: Recite Surah al-Qadr (chapter 97) after Fajr, up to 50 times.
Pregnancy.body: Recommended every day of the pregnancy as a means of blessing and protection.
Pregnancy.src: A Mother’s Prayer, ch.2, prayer 5; From Marriage to Parenthood, p.116

Pregnancy.title: Surah al-Fatiha (continuous)
Pregnancy.translit: Keep Surah al-Fatiha on your tongue.
Pregnancy.body: Reciting Surah al-Fatiha regularly through the whole pregnancy is recommended for the wellbeing of mother and child.

Pregnancy.title: Ayah for the child (Yasin 36:36)
Pregnancy.translit: Recite verse 36 of Surah Yasin forty times over a glass of water, then drink it.
Pregnancy.body: Every day, for forty days in a row.

Easy delivery.title: Surah al-Inshiqaq
Easy delivery.translit: Recite Surah al-Inshiqaq (chapter 84) after each prayer in the ninth month, and when labour starts.
Easy delivery.body: If you cannot say it aloud in labour, recite it in your head.

Easy delivery.title: Du’a for ease
Easy delivery.arabic: رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي
Easy delivery.translit: Rabbi-shraḥ lī ṣadrī wa yassir lī amrī
Easy delivery.body: “My Lord, expand for me my chest and ease for me my task.” A beautiful du’a for calm and ease in labour.

Easy delivery.title: Recitations for a hard labour
Easy delivery.translit: Qurʾān 94:5–6, 46:35 and 79:46, recited or written for the mother.
Easy delivery.body: Imam ʿAlī (as) gave 94:5–6 for a hard labour, and Imam al-Ṣādiq (as) 46:35 and 79:46. A companion may recite them over you.
Easy delivery.src: Ṭibb al-Aʾimmah, via duas.org; A Mother’s Prayer, ch.4, prayers 1, 6 and 8, which have them written and tied on

Easy delivery.title: Eating dates
Easy delivery.translit: Keep dates to hand as delivery nears.
Easy delivery.body: Echoing the words to Maryam (as): “Shake the trunk of the palm tree towards you, it will drop fresh, ripe dates.” Dates give gentle, natural energy.
Easy delivery.src: Qurʾān 19:25; al-Kāfī, Vol. 6, Kitāb al-ʿAqīqah, ch.12 ḥ.3–4

Easy delivery.title: Sadaqah before delivery
Easy delivery.translit: Give charity with the niyyah of a safe birth.
Easy delivery.body: Imam al-Ṣādiq (as) said charity repels misfortune and a bad death.
Easy delivery.src: al-Kāfī, Vol. 4, Kitāb al-Zakāt, “Charity repels misfortune”

Easy delivery.title: Surah Maryam over the mother
Easy delivery.translit: Recite Surah Maryam 19:23–25 over the mother.
Easy delivery.body: Imam al-Bāqir (as) told a companion whose wife was in a hard labour to recite these verses over her, recalling Maryam (as) at the moment of delivery.
Easy delivery.src: Ṭibb al-Aʾimmah (Imam al-Bāqir), via duas.org; A Mother’s Prayer, ch.4, prayer 2

Easy delivery.title: Du’a Yastashir (9th month)
Easy delivery.translit: Recite the supplication of Yastashir daily in the ninth month.
Easy delivery.body: A supplication of praise recommended regularly through pregnancy, and every day in the ninth month, for ease as delivery approaches.

After birth.title: Adhan & Iqamah
After birth.translit: Adhan in the baby’s right ear, Iqamah in the left.
After birth.body: Adhān in the right ear and iqāmah in the left, ideally before the cord is cut. The Prophet (s) called it a protection from Satan.
After birth.src: al-Kāfī, Vol. 6, Kitāb al-ʿAqīqah, ch.13 ḥ.1, 6

After birth.title: Tahnik
After birth.translit: Touch the baby’s palate with a trace of Euphrates water and turbah of Imam Ḥusayn (as), or a softened date.
After birth.body: The Imams (as) recommended Euphrates water and the turbah of Imam Ḥusayn (as), or rain water if these are not to hand; the Prophet (s) used a date for al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn (as). Only a trace. Never honey: the NHS advises no honey before age one, because of infant botulism.
After birth.src: al-Kāfī, Vol. 6, Kitāb al-ʿAqīqah, ch.13 ḥ.3–5; A Mother’s Prayer, ch.6, act 3

After birth.title: A good name
After birth.body: Giving a good name is among the first rights of the child. See the Baby names section for suggestions honouring the Ahlulbayt (as).
After birth.src: al-Kāfī, Vol. 6, Kitāb al-ʿAqīqah, ch.10 ḥ.3; ch.34 ḥ.1

After birth.title: Aqiqah
After birth.translit: Perform the aqiqah, ideally on the 7th day.
After birth.body: A highly recommended sacrifice on the seventh day. Shave the baby’s head first and give its weight in silver or gold as ṣadaqah, then the ʿaqīqah; the midwife is given a share of the meat, and the parents should not eat from it.
After birth.src: al-Kāfī, Vol. 6, Kitāb al-ʿAqīqah, ch.14 ḥ.9; ch.17 ḥ.1, 6; A Mother’s Prayer, ch.6, acts 6 and 8

After birth.title: Du’a of shukr
After birth.translit: Sajdat al-shukr: forehead to the ground, “shukran lillāh”.
After birth.body: A prostration of thanks for a safe delivery and the gift of your child.

After birth.title: Prayers for breastfeeding
After birth.translit: Recite in gratitude and ask for barakah in your milk.
After birth.body: Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) said no milk carries more blessing for a child than its mother’s. Say Bismillāh before each feed, ask Allah to bless your milk, and pair it with rest, water and duʿāʾ.
After birth.src: al-Kāfī, Vol. 6, Kitāb al-ʿAqīqah, ch.28 ḥ.1; A Mother’s Prayer, ch.5

Daily dhikr.title: Tasbih of Sayyida Fatima (as)
Daily dhikr.body: Recited after each of the five daily prayers — a gift from the Prophet (s) to his daughter (as), full of reward.
Daily dhikr.src: al-Kāfī, Vol. 3, Kitāb al-Ṣalāh, ḥ.8–9; Sistani, Islamic Laws, ruling 1108

Daily dhikr.title: Salawat
Daily dhikr.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِ مُحَمَّدٍ
Daily dhikr.translit: Allahumma salli ‘ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad.
Daily dhikr.body: Sending blessings on the Prophet and his family, a light for you and your baby. Always include the family.

Daily dhikr.title: SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi
Daily dhikr.body: Imam al-Ṣādiq (as) said whoever says this thirty times turns away poverty and knocks on the door of Paradise.

Daily dhikr.title: Istighfar
Daily dhikr.body: Seeking forgiveness softens the heart and invites mercy and ease.
Daily dhikr.src: Man lā yaḥḍuruhu al-faqīh, Vol. 1, ḥ.1405; al-Kāfī, Vol. 2, Kitāb al-Duʿāʾ

salawat.ar: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِ مُحَمَّدٍ
salawat.tl: Allāhumma ṣalli ʿalā Muḥammadin wa Āli Muḥammad
salawat.en: O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.
salawat.sr: Blessings on the Prophet (s) always include his family (al-Amālī of al-Ṣadūq, majlis 60, ḥ.6).

salawat-long.ar: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَجِّلْ فَرَجَهُمْ وَأَهْلِكْ عَدُوَّهُمْ مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِينَ وَالْآخِرِينَ
salawat-long.tl: Allāhumma ṣalli ʿalā Muḥammadin wa Āli Muḥammad, wa ʿajjil farajahum, wa ahlik ʿaduwwahum minal-jinni wal-insi minal-awwalīna wal-ākhirīn
salawat-long.en: O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their relief, and destroy their enemies from among the jinn and humankind, from the first of them to the last.
salawat-long.sr: ʿAllāmah Majlisī, Biḥār al-Anwār, Vol. 86, p.289: recommended often from Thursday ʿAṣr to the end of Friday. Reciting it with your hand on your stomach: From Marriage to Parenthood, p.110.

istighfar.en: I seek forgiveness from Allah, my Lord, and I turn to Him in repentance.
istighfar.sr: The Prophet (s) sought forgiveness seventy times a day (al-Kāfī, Vol. 2, p.505).

tasbih.ar: اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ ٣٤ · الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٣٣ · سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ ٣٣
tasbih.en: Allah is the Greatest (34), All praise belongs to Allah (33), Glory be to Allah (33).
tasbih.sr: A gift from the Prophet (s) to his daughter (as), recited after every ṣalāh (al-Kāfī, Vol. 3, Kitāb al-Ṣalāh; Sistani, ruling 1108).

DUA_TODAY.arabic: رَبِّ هَبْ لِي مِنْ لَدُنْكَ ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةً ۖ إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ الدُّعَاءِ
DUA_TODAY.tl: Rabbi hab lī min ladunka dhurriyyatan ṭayyibah, innaka samīʿud-duʿāʾ
DUA_TODAY.mn: “My Lord! Grant me a good offspring from You! Indeed You hear all supplications.”
DUA_TODAY.sr: Sūrah Āl ʿImrān 3:38 · From Marriage to Parenthood, p.117

DUA_TODAY.arabic: رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ وَاجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَامًا
DUA_TODAY.tl: Rabbanā hab lanā min azwājinā wa dhurriyyātinā qurrata aʿyunin wajʿalnā lil-muttaqīna imāmā
DUA_TODAY.mn: “Our Lord! Give us joy and comfort in our spouses and offspring, and make us imams of the Godwary.”
DUA_TODAY.sr: Sūrah al-Furqān 25:74 · From Marriage to Parenthood, p.118

DUA_TODAY.mn: “My Lord! Give me [an heir], one of the righteous.”
DUA_TODAY.sr: Sūrah aṣ-Ṣāffāt 37:100 · From Marriage to Parenthood, p.117

DUA_TODAY.arabic: رَبِّ اجْعَلْنِي مُقِيمَ الصَّلَاةِ وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي ۚ رَبَّنَا وَتَقَبَّلْ دُعَاءِ
DUA_TODAY.tl: Rabbi-jʿalnī muqīmaṣ-ṣalāti wa min dhurriyyatī, Rabbanā wa taqabbal duʿāʾ
DUA_TODAY.mn: “My Lord! Make me a maintainer of prayer, and my descendants [as well]. Our Lord, accept my supplication.”
DUA_TODAY.sr: Sūrah Ibrāhīm 14:40 · From Marriage to Parenthood, p.118

DUA_TODAY.arabic: رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِي أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَالِدَيَّ وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صَالِحًا تَرْضَاهُ وَأَصْلِحْ لِي فِي ذُرِّيَّتِي
DUA_TODAY.tl: Rabbi awziʿnī an ashkura niʿmatakallatī anʿamta ʿalayya wa ʿalā wālidayya wa an aʿmala ṣāliḥan tarḍāhu wa aṣliḥ lī fī dhurriyyatī
DUA_TODAY.mn: “My Lord! Inspire me to give thanks for Your blessing with which You have blessed me and my parents, and that I may do righteous deeds which please You, and invest my descendants with righteousness.”
DUA_TODAY.sr: Sūrah al-Aḥqāf 46:15 · From Marriage to Parenthood, p.118

DUA_TODAY.arabic: رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي
DUA_TODAY.tl: Rabbi-shraḥ lī ṣadrī wa yassir lī amrī
DUA_TODAY.mn: “My Lord! Open my breast for me. Make my task easy for me.”

DUA_TODAY.arabic: وَإِنِّي أُعِيذُهَا بِكَ وَذُرِّيَّتَهَا مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ
DUA_TODAY.tl: Wa innī uʿīdhuhā bika wa dhurriyyatahā minash-shayṭānir-rajīm
DUA_TODAY.mn: “I commend her and her offspring to Your care against [the evil of] the outcast Satan.” The prayer of the mother of Maryam (as).

DUA_TODAY.arabic: فَإِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا ۝ إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا
DUA_TODAY.tl: Fa-inna maʿal-ʿusri yusrā, inna maʿal-ʿusri yusrā
DUA_TODAY.mn: “Indeed ease accompanies hardship. Indeed ease accompanies hardship.” A verse to hold onto in the hardest moments of pregnancy and labour.
DUA_TODAY.sr: Sūrah ash-Sharḥ 94:5–6 · for a hard labour: Imam ʿAlī (as) in Ṭibb al-Aʾimmah; A Mother’s Prayer, ch.4, prayer 8

BISMILLAH.en: In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful.

2:255.ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلْحَىُّ ٱلْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُۥ سِنَةٌۭ وَلَا نَوْمٌۭ ۚ لَّهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِى يَشْفَعُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِۦ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَىْءٍۢ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِۦٓ إِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَـُٔودُهُۥ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَلِىُّ ٱلْعَظِيمُ
2:255.tl: Allahu laaa ilaaha illaa Huwal Haiyul Qaiyoom; laa taakhuzuhoo sinatunw wa laa nawm; lahoo maa fissamaawaati wa maa fil ard; man zal lazee yashfa'u 'indahooo illaa bi-iznih; ya'lamu maa baina aydeehim wa maa khalfahum wa laa yuheetoona bishai'im min 'ilmihee illaa bimaa shaaa'; wasi'a Kursiyyuhus samaawaati wal arda wa laa ya'ooduhoo hifzuhumaa; wa Huwal 'Aliyyul 'Azeem
2:255.en: Allah—there is no god except Him—is the Living One, the All-sustainer. Neither drowsiness befalls Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that may intercede with Him except with His permission? He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not comprehend anything of His knowledge except what He wishes. His seat embraces the heavens and the earth and He is not wearied by their preservation, and He is the All-exalted, the All-supreme.

3:36.ar: فَلَمَّا وَضَعَتْهَا قَالَتْ رَبِّ إِنِّى وَضَعْتُهَآ أُنثَىٰ وَٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا وَضَعَتْ وَلَيْسَ ٱلذَّكَرُ كَٱلْأُنثَىٰ ۖ وَإِنِّى سَمَّيْتُهَا مَرْيَمَ وَإِنِّىٓ أُعِيذُهَا بِكَ وَذُرِّيَّتَهَا مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ
3:36.tl: Falammaa wada'at-haa qaalat Rabbi innee wada'tuhaaa unsaa wallaahu a'lamu bimaa wada'at wa laisaz zakaru kalunsaa wa innee sammaituhaa Maryama wa innee u'eezuhaa bika wa zurriyyatahaa minash Shaitaanir Rajeem
3:36.en: When she bore her, she said, ‘My Lord, I have borne a female [child]’—and Allah knew better what she had borne, and the male [child she expected] was no match for the female [child she had borne] —‘and I have named her Mary, and I commend her and her offspring to Your care against [the evil of] the outcast Satan.’

3:38.ar: هُنَالِكَ دَعَا زَكَرِيَّا رَبَّهُۥ ۖ قَالَ رَبِّ هَبْ لِى مِن لَّدُنكَ ذُرِّيَّةًۭ طَيِّبَةً ۖ إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ ٱلدُّعَآءِ
3:38.tl: Hunaalika da'aa Zakariyyaa Rabbahoo qaala Rabbi hab lee mil ladunka zurriyyatan taiyibatan innaka samee'ud du'aaa'
3:38.en: Thereat Zechariah supplicated his Lord. He said, ‘My Lord! Grant me a good offspring from You! Indeed You hear all supplications.’

14:40.ar: رَبِّ ٱجْعَلْنِى مُقِيمَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِى ۚ رَبَّنَا وَتَقَبَّلْ دُعَآءِ
14:40.tl: Rabbij 'alnee muqeemas Salaati wa min zurriyyatee Rabbanaa wa taqabbal du'aaa'
14:40.en: My Lord! Make me a maintainer of prayer, and my descendants [as well]. Our Lord, accept my supplication.

16:69.ar: ثُمَّ كُلِى مِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ فَٱسْلُكِى سُبُلَ رَبِّكِ ذُلُلًۭا ۚ يَخْرُجُ مِنۢ بُطُونِهَا شَرَابٌۭ مُّخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوَٰنُهُۥ فِيهِ شِفَآءٌۭ لِّلنَّاسِ ۗ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَةًۭ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
16:69.tl: Summa kulee min kullis samaraati faslukee subula Rabbiki zululaa; yakhruju mim butoonihaa sharaabum mukhtalifun alwaanuhoo feehi shifaaa'ul linnaas, inna fee zaalika la-aayatal liqawminy yatafakkaroon
16:69.en: Then eat from every [kind of] fruit and follow meekly the ways of your Lord. There issues from its belly a juice of diverse hues, in which there is a cure for the people. There is indeed a sign in that for a people who reflect.

19:25.ar: وَهُزِّىٓ إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ ٱلنَّخْلَةِ تُسَٰقِطْ عَلَيْكِ رُطَبًۭا جَنِيًّۭا
19:25.tl: Wa huzzeee ilaiki bijiz'in nakhlati tusaaqit 'alaiki rutaban janiyyaa
19:25.en: Shake the trunk of the palm tree, freshly picked dates will drop upon you.

20:25.en: He said, ‘My Lord! Open my breast for me.

20:26.en: Make my task easy for me.

25:74.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَٰجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّٰتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍۢ وَٱجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَامًا
25:74.tl: Wallazeena yaqooloona Rabbanaa hab lanaa min azwaajinaa wa zurriyaatinaa qurrata a'yuninw waj 'alnaa lilmuttaqeena Imaamaa
25:74.en: And those who say, ‘Our Lord! Give us joy and comfort in our spouses and offspring, and make us imams of the Godwary.’

36:36.ar: سُبْحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلْأَزْوَٰجَ كُلَّهَا مِمَّا تُنۢبِتُ ٱلْأَرْضُ وَمِنْ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَمِمَّا لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
36:36.tl: Subhaanal lazee khalaqal azwaaja kullahaa mimmaa tumbitul ardu wa min anfusihim wa mimmaa laa ya'lamoon
36:36.en: Immaculate is He who has created all the kinds of what the earth grows, and of themselves, and of what they do not know.

37:100.en: ‘My Lord! Give me [an heir], one of the righteous.’

46:15.ar: وَوَصَّيْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ بِوَٰلِدَيْهِ إِحْسَٰنًا ۖ حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُۥ كُرْهًۭا وَوَضَعَتْهُ كُرْهًۭا ۖ وَحَمْلُهُۥ وَفِصَٰلُهُۥ ثَلَٰثُونَ شَهْرًا ۚ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُۥ وَبَلَغَ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةًۭ قَالَ رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِىٓ أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَىَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَٰلِدَىَّ وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صَٰلِحًۭا تَرْضَىٰهُ وَأَصْلِحْ لِى فِى ذُرِّيَّتِىٓ ۖ إِنِّى تُبْتُ إِلَيْكَ وَإِنِّى مِنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ
46:15.tl: Wa wassainal insaana biwaalidaihi ihsaanan hamalathu ummuhoo kurhanw-wa wada'athu kurhanw wa hamluhoo wa fisaaluhoo salaasoona shahraa; hattaaa izaa balagha ashuddahoo wa balagha arba'eena sanatan qaala Rabbi awzi'neee an ashkura ni'matakal lateee an'amta 'alaiya wa 'alaa waalidaiya wa an a'mala saalihan tardaahu wa aslih lee fee zurriyyatee innee tubtu ilaika wa innee minal muslimeen
46:15.en: We have enjoined man to be kind to his parents. His mother has carried him in travail, and bore him in travail, and his gestation and weaning take thirty months. When he comes of age and reaches forty years, he says, ‘My Lord! Inspire me to give thanks for Your blessing with which You have blessed me and my parents, and that I may do righteous deeds which please You, and invest my descendants with righteousness. Indeed I have turned to you in penitence, and I am one of the Muslims.’

v.en: In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful.
All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of all the worlds,
the All-beneficent, the All-merciful,
Master of the Day of Retribution.
You [alone] do we worship, and to You [alone] do we turn for help.
Guide us on the straight path,

v.ar: صِرَٰطَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
v.en: the path of those whom You have blessed — such as have not incurred Your wrath, nor are astray.
By the fig and the olive,
by Mount Sinai,
and by this secure town:

v.ar: لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ فِىٓ أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍۢ
v.tl: Laqad khalaqnal insaana fee ahsani taqweem
v.en: We certainly created man in the best of forms;
then We relegated him to the lowest of the low,

v.ar: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍۢ
v.tl: Illal lazeena aamanoo wa 'amilus saalihaati falahum ajrun ghairu mamnoon
v.en: except those who have faith and do righteous deeds. There will be an everlasting reward for them.
So what makes you deny the Retribution?
Is not Allah the fairest of all judges?
Indeed We sent it down on the Night of Ordainment.

v.tl: Wa maaa adraaka maa lailatul qadr
v.en: And what will show you what is the Night of Ordainment?

v.ar: لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌۭ مِّنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍۢ
v.tl: Lailatul qadri khairum min alfi shahr
v.en: The Night of Ordainment is better than a thousand months.

v.ar: تَنَزَّلُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ فِيهَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِم مِّن كُلِّ أَمْرٍۢ
v.tl: Tanazzalul malaaa'ikatu war roohu feehaa bi-izni Rabbihim min kulli amr
v.en: In it the angels and the Spirit descend, by the leave of their Lord, with every command.
It is peaceful until the rising of the dawn.
By Time!
Man is indeed in loss,

v.ar: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ
v.tl: Illal lazeena aamanoo wa 'amilus saalihaati wa tawaasaw bil haqqi wa tawaasaw bis sabr
v.en: except those who have faith and do righteous deeds, and enjoin one another to [follow] the truth, and enjoin one another to patience.
Indeed We have given you abundance.
So pray to your Lord, and sacrifice [the sacrificial camel].
Indeed it is your enemy who is without posterity.

v.tl: Izaa jaaa'a nasrul laahi wal fath
v.en: When Allah’s help comes with victory,

v.ar: وَرَأَيْتَ ٱلنَّاسَ يَدْخُلُونَ فِى دِينِ ٱللَّهِ أَفْوَاجًۭا
v.tl: Wa ra-aitan naasa yadkhuloona fee deenil laahi afwaajaa
v.en: and you see the people entering Allah’s religion in throngs,

v.ar: فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَٱسْتَغْفِرْهُ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ تَوَّابًۢا
v.tl: Fasabbih bihamdi Rabbika wastaghfirhu, innahoo kaana tawwaabaa
v.en: celebrate the praise of your Lord, and plead to Him for forgiveness. Indeed, He is all-clement.
Say, ‘He is Allah, the One.
Allah is the All-embracing.
He neither begat, nor was begotten,
nor has He any equal.’

BASE_TASKS.t: Pray your daily ṣalāh on time
BASE_TASKS.s: A steady anchor through your day.
6 to 8 glasses today, more if it is hot.
A short walk or a stretch eases the aches.
